name: Helix Biosystems Cortical Patience Engine
description: The Cortical Patience Engine is a cognitive augmentation that addresses one of the most consistent failure points in high-stakes human decision-making: the compression of perceived time during stress. By modulating activity in the prefrontal cortex and anterior cingulate through a network of precision-placed inductive microstimulators — seventeen nodes distributed across the skull's inner surface — the Engine selectively dilates subjective time perception during elevated cortisol and adrenaline states, giving the user what operators describe as 'room to think inside the moment.' The effect is not a reflex boost; the body does not move faster. Instead, the mind processes incoming information more completely before committing to a response.
specifications: {"stimulation_nodes":"17","time_dilation_factor":"2.4–3.1× subjective time expansion during activation","activation_trigger":"Cortisol spike above 22 nmol/L or manual override","duration_per_episode":"Up to 8 minutes subjective (approx. 2.5 minutes objective)","cooldown_period":"14 minutes between full activations","power_draw":"Passive 0.4W baseline; 2.1W during active dilation","side_effects":"Post-activation fatigue, minor temporal dysphoria, reported dream fragmentation"}
cultural_context: Helix Biosystems has positioned the Cortical Patience Engine as a tool for 'executive cognitive performance' — and in GLMZ's upper corporate tiers, it has become something of a prestige augmentation among senior decision-makers who would never admit to carrying combat-relevant hardware. The social mythology around it is that its users are simply calm, measured, unhurried people — naturally gifted with patience. This fiction is carefully maintained. In lower districts, a cruder reputation has formed: users are called 'clockeaters,' and the belief that someone running the Engine is fundamentally not operating in the same moment as you produces a distinct unease in those who know what to look for.
known_users: High-stakes gamblers in augmented game circuits
Interrogation specialists in corporate intelligence divisions
story_hooks: A labor negotiation has gone inexplicably well for the corporation every single time, across multiple union representatives and three years — someone finally notices the corporate arbiter always has the same subtle post-session fatigue.

A clockeater has been running the Engine beyond safe parameters, pushing the cooldown and stacking sessions — the temporal dysphoria has progressed to the point where they can no longer reliably tell if they are in an activated state or not.

Helix Biosystems' restriction agreement includes a clause that allows them to pull activation logs from the Engine — a whistleblower has obtained logs from a city official's unit that document exactly what decisions they 'took their time' on.

The Engine's cortisol trigger has malfunctioned in a user, activating during sleep — they are now spending hours of subjective time trapped in slow-motion nightmares while their body rests for minutes.
